newsitem.title: UK: UK's Independent newspaper circulation down 8 pct.
newsitem.headline: UK's Independent newspaper circulation down 8 pct.

text.p: Britain's Independent newspaper saw its average daily circulation fall 8.04 percent in the first half of 1997 compared to first six months of 1996, while the UK's four other national broadsheet newspapers all posted gains, the UK's Audit Bureau of Circulation said on Friday.

Circulation of the Independent, jointly owned by Mirror Group Plc and Ireland's Independent Newspapers Plc, fell to 257,010 in the first six months of 1997 from 279,473 a year earlier, the Audit Bureau said in its monthly report.
The Times, part of News Corp Ltd, posted a 9.22 percent circulation gain in the 1997 first-half, up to 747,710 from 684,605 in the 1996 period.

The Daily Telegraph, owned by Canada's Hollinger Inc and Britain's largest-circulating quality newspaper, saw circulation rise 7.76 percent to 1,124,640 in the 1997 first-half from 1,043,677 in the 1996 period, the Audit Bureau reported.
The Financial Times, part of Pearson Plc, posted a 3.56 percent circulation gain to 312,723, while the Guardian's circulation rose 2.70 percent to 408,790 in the 1997 first half.
